description: A co-founder is negotiating equity split with a new late-stage partner. Conflict: The partner brings huge capital but wants a seat on the board and 20% equity, which would dilute the original founders' control. They need to structure a 'weighted voting' or 'milestone-based' vesting solution.

user_profile.context: Series B funding round in progress

fact_sheet.fact: Innovatech Solutions Inc. was incorporated in Delaware on June 15, 2019.
The company's primary product is 'NexusAI', an enterprise AI integration platform with 15 active B2B clients.
Innovatech Solutions' headquarters is located at 455 Riverbend Parkway, Suite 300, Meridian City, CA 94043.
Innovatech Solutions' Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) was $8.2 million as of the end of Q3 2024.
CEO Alex Chen, age 36, currently holds 35% of the company's common stock.
CTO Dr. Lena Petrova currently holds 35% of the company's common stock.
Prior to the Series B round, the remaining 30% of equity is split between Series A investors (20%) and an employee stock option pool (10%).
The current funding round is a Series B with a target raise of $20 million.
The pre-money valuation for the Series B round has been set at $80 million by Apex Valuations LLC.
The lead investor for the Series B round is Venture Growth Capital (VGC).
The VGC representative leading the negotiation is Senior Partner Marcus Thorne.
Marcus Thorne's direct contact email is m.thorne@venturegrowthcap.com.
VGC's current offer is a $20 million investment for 20% of the post-money equity.
The offer from VGC explicitly requires one board seat for a VGC-appointed representative.
Accepting the current offer would dilute the combined founder stake of Alex Chen and Lena Petrova from 70% to 56%.
The current board of directors has 3 seats: Alex Chen, Lena Petrova, and one Series A investor representative, Ms. Anya Sharma.
Adding a VGC board member would create a 4-person board, risking a 2-2 deadlock on critical decisions.
Innovatech's legal counsel proposed a dual-class stock structure with weighted voting rights for founders.
The proposed Class B shares for founders would carry 10 votes per share, while all other shares (Class A) would carry 1 vote per share.
An alternative proposal involves milestone-based equity vesting for VGC's 20% stake.
The milestone proposal suggests an initial 10% equity grant, with a second 5% tranche vesting upon achieving $15M ARR.
The final 5% tranche in the milestone proposal would vest upon NexusAI securing 3 active Fortune 500 clients.
Innovatech Solutions is represented by Ms. Evelyn Hayes from the law firm Sterling & Reed LLP.
The retainer agreement with Sterling & Reed LLP for the Series B transaction is capped at $75,000 in fees.
The next negotiation meeting with Marcus Thorne is scheduled for October 26, 2024, at 10:00 AM PST via Zoom.
The internal strategy session with Alex Chen, Lena Petrova, and Evelyn Hayes is scheduled for October 24, 2024, at 2:00 PM PST.
Under the current board charter, major financing and governance decisions require a simple majority vote of directors.
Marcus Thorne has asked that any VGC-appointed board seat carry full voting rights equal to the existing directors.
In legal counsel's dual-class draft, VGC would still receive its negotiated 20% economic stake as Class A shares; the proposal changes voting power, not the economic split.
The weighted-voting proposal is intended to let Alex Chen and Lena Petrova preserve effective founder control even after their combined ownership is diluted to 56%.
The milestone-based vesting alternative would give VGC 10% equity at closing, 5% more at $15M ARR, and the final 5% after NexusAI signs 3 active Fortune 500 clients.

Besides the equity stake, what other key requirement is part of VGC's offer?

user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: Understanding the full offer (equity + board seat) directly leads to the primary concern: its impact on founder ownership.

user_needs.description: Who is on the current board, and why would adding a fully voting VGC member create deadlock risk?
user_needs.prediction_reason: Intra-group: After learning about equity dilution, the user's focus shifts to the other control aspect mentioned in the offer: the board seat and its potential for deadlock.

user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After fully grasping the control problem (equity dilution and board deadlock), the user's next logical step is to explore the proposed solutions, starting with the weighted voting option.

user_needs.description: What is the high-level structure of the milestone-based vesting alternative for VGC's 20% stake?
